values:
1. It is difficult to maintain daily routine of meditation and satsang expecially when not being in frequent touch of ashrams.
2. There is no one stop platform for knowing about all the events happening in our spiritual school.
3. It is difficult to get access to and comprehend gurumaharaj's literature.
4. New generations are not able to understand the value of gurumaharaj's teachings and research, hence don't follow or participate in it.
To preserve Gurumaharaj’s legacy and pass his teachings on to future generations.
To use technology in our spiritual school to help disciples stay regular in meditation and satsang, remain aware, connected, and actively involved.

1. It is difficult to follow a daily routine of meditation and satsang, especially when we are not regularly connected with the ashrams.
2. There is no single platform where disciples can find information about all the events and activities happening in our spiritual school.
3. Gurumaharaj’s literature can be difficult to access, read, and understand.
4. The younger generation often does not fully understand the importance of Gurumaharaj’s teachings and research, which leads to less participation and connection with the spiritual tradition.
5. To make Gurumaharaj’s teachings more relevant and meaningful to the younger generation by showing how they can be useful in today’s world.

Technical development: Ajay Bhatnagar
Digital Marketing: Ayushi & Vaishnav Bhatnagar
Product Management: Tejaswini Venkata

Visual simplification, light/dark mode, daily quote scheduling and archive, deep-link sharing, analytics/admin dashboard, audio seeking, stronger account controls, and meditation/session reliability fixes.
Flutter analysis passed; 27 tests passed; AAB package/version/signature validated.

values: Everything listed here was completed or prepared in Version 0 of the Guruvandan app.
Device app name shows Guru Vandan
Android, iOS, and web manifest naming updated.
Users see the correct devotional app name.
The shared Guru Vandan logo replaced the default Flutter icon.
The app feels official and recognizable.
Crimson, off-white, soft gold, and calm devotional styling used throughout.
The interface feels aligned with the spiritual school.
Large text, simple actions, and spacious controls.
Older devotees can use the app with less confusion.
User chooses English or Hindi before authentication.
The app starts in the user's preferred language.
Language can be changed later from the More page.
Google authentication flow added through Firebase.
Users can enter the app quickly with Google.
Phone number and OTP flow added.
Users without Google login can still sign in.
Known users are not asked for name again after login.
First name, middle name, and last name captured separately.
Profiles are cleaner and easier to personalize.
Greeting uses first name instead of full name.
The home screen feels personal without being crowded.
User can update name from the More page.
Wrong or changed names can be corrected.
Shown after new user signup/name setup.
First entry feels warm and ceremonial.
Morning, Evening, and Dhyan quick buttons
Home cards navigate to their correct tabs/pages.
Main routines are reachable in one tap.
About Guru Maharaj and About Guru Vandan content added.
Important context is present without overwhelming the home page.
Satsang, aarti, and meditation completion can be tracked.
Devotees can see their daily spiritual practice progress.
Morning satsang audio is inside the APK assets.
No waiting for download before playback.
Shaam satsang audio is inside the APK assets.
Evening satsang works directly from the app.
Separate Aarti tab added with bundled Aarti audio.
Aarti has its own clear place.
Playback progress and total duration are shown.
Users understand where they are in the satsang.
User can mark satsang and aarti as complete.
Popup asks user to put phone on silent before satsang or meditation starts.
Satsang, meditation, and Om continue when app is minimized.
Audio does not stop during practice.
Users can start common sessions quickly.
Longer or personal durations are supported.
Users stay in control of the session.
Chant plays only when timer ends
Opening chant was removed; closing chant plays after timed meditation.
Meditation time remains pure and uninterrupted.
Om audio can play endlessly when no meditation timer is running.
Users can listen for calm focus outside timer sessions.
If timer is running, Om stops before the closing chant plays.
Streak depends only on daily meditation continuity.
Users are encouraged to meditate daily.
Current, best, and total meditation days
Streak area explains continuity, not duration.
The meaning of the streak is easy to understand.
Wisdom page loads all admin-uploaded quotes when online.
New wisdom appears without rebuilding the app.
Admin quotes are ordered newest first.
Fresh content is easy to find.
Quote language follows the selected app language.
Devotees get wisdom in their chosen language.
Quote sharing includes the quote text and app link.
Users can share Sadguru wisdom through phone apps.
Wisdom page shows loaded quote count
Shows how many quotes are available.
Admin can verify content is reaching the app.
Shop, Events, Guru Gallery, and Jigyasa
Coming soon modules are placed inside More.
Future features are visible without cluttering core tabs.
Logout returns user to the sign-in flow.
Shared devices can be signed out cleanly.
Admin page moved to separate route
Admin is accessed through the admin URL only.
Normal users do not see admin tools in More.
Admin can enter English and Hindi quote text and attribution.
Spiritual content can be updated manually.
Already uploaded quotes can be edited.
Mistakes can be corrected without database work.
Admin can view user activity in chart and text form.
Firebase Auth is used for Google and phone login.
The app has real account-based access.
Users, quotes, routines, and activity are stored in Firebase Realtime Database.
Admin changes can appear dynamically in the app.
Latest Android APK is ready for install and sharing.
The app can be tested on Android devices.
Live web app is deployed for browser review.
The work can be shared with the team instantly.
iOS project files are ready for Mac or cloud compilation.
The next step can happen on Mac/cloud without rebuilding from scratch.

values: Completed work through Android release 1.0.28 (31), including the three latest reliability fixes.
Refreshed cards, typography, spacing, navigation, and devotional colors across the app.
A cleaner and more consistent experience on Android and iOS.
Long supporting copy was removed where a clear section heading already communicates the purpose.
Screens are easier to scan and feel less crowded.
Users can change the visual theme from the app.
Comfortable viewing in bright and low-light settings.
Footer labels and icons use high-contrast colors in dark mode.
Daily Sacred Practice moved above streak
The primary daily action appears before continuity statistics.
Users reach the daily routine faster.
Yesterday streak hidden for first-time users
The previous-day indicator is omitted until the user has relevant history.
New users are not shown misleading streak data.
Previous Sadguru Maharaj wording was replaced throughout relevant app sections.
Attribution is consistent with the approved name.
The Hindi devotional-store wording was updated to Satsang Samigri.
The label matches the requested terminology.
Only the quote assigned to the current date is presented as the daily quote.
Users receive a focused daily teaching.
Newly uploaded quotes fill upcoming dates in sequence.
Administrators can prepare many days of content in advance.
Quotes move into the archive after their scheduled day.
Shared links carry a quote identifier and route the installed app to that quote.
Recipients land directly on the intended teaching.
Shared quote links provide Google Play and App Store destinations when the app is unavailable.
Recipients can install the correct app for their device.
Quote sharing includes branded text, attribution, and a web/deep link.
Shared content is recognizable and actionable.
Quote likes are stored and included in analytics.
Users can drag the playback position backward or forward.
Listeners can repeat or skip to a chosen part.
Aarti playback supports direct position seeking.
Users have consistent controls across audio sections.
Key navigation and app lifecycle events are recorded in Firebase.
The team can understand adoption and screen usage.
Actual satsang and aarti playback time is recorded.
The admin portal can report real listening engagement.
Meditation starts, elapsed time, and successful completions are tracked.
The team can compare intent with completed practice.
Wisdom interactions are captured as structured events.
The team can see which content users value.
A responsive Firebase-hosted admin page is protected by administrator email/password authentication.
Authorized staff can manage the app from a phone or browser.
The portal shows what each user did and when.
Support and engagement review can be user-specific.
Aggregate totals, seven-day activity, and activity breakdowns are visualized.
Overall app usage is understandable at a glance.
Administrators can add, edit, schedule, and review quote content.
Daily wisdom can be maintained without an app release.
Database access rules protect administration and user activity data.
The privacy page documents app activity collection and its operational purpose.
Users and reviewers receive clearer data-use information.
Apple authentication is integrated for supported devices.
iOS users have a platform-native login option.
Existing identities can be linked when the same account uses another provider.
Users can permanently delete their account and associated records, including provider revocation handling.
Account controls meet user and store expectations.
A valid Google/Firebase session is restored before showing sign-in after the app is closed.
Closing the app no longer signs the user out.
Timed Om playback now reaches the selected endpoint, plays the ending chant, and shows the completion message once.
Users receive the expected end-of-session confirmation.
Correct timer duration in media controls
The media source presented to Android uses the selected meditation duration instead of the full Om recording length.
A one-minute session displays as one minute on the lock screen.
Version 1.0.28 with version code 31 was built, signed, and validated as an Android App Bundle.
The corrected build is ready for internal testing upload.
Static analysis, tests, and bundle validation
Flutter analysis passed, 27 automated tests passed, and the AAB manifest/signature were verified.
The release has repeatable technical checks before testing.

Timed playback now ends at the selected duration and runs the normal completion flow.
Automated tests and release build passed; confirm once on an internal-test device.
A one-minute meditation appeared as roughly three hours on the lock screen.
Android media metadata now exposes the selected timer duration instead of the source recording duration.
AAB metadata/signature verified; confirm the media notification on a physical Android device.
Closing and reopening the app logged the user out.
The app silently restores a valid Google/Firebase session before showing the sign-in screen.
Authentication flow compiles and tests pass; confirm session persistence through internal testing.
